words.definition: careful to avoid danger or mistakes

hero.text: Juniper was cautious on the icy rooftop, testing each step before putting her weight down.

words.everyday: Grandpa is cautious at the busy corner and looks both ways twice before crossing.

contrast.nonExample: Theo raced down the steep hill on his bike without touching the brakes.
contrast.explanation: Cautious people slow down and think about danger first. Theo rushed ahead without any care, so he was reckless, not cautious.

items.prompt: Which person is being cautious?

options.text: Mila taps the pond ice with a stick before stepping on it.
Jon dashes straight onto the frozen pond without looking first or checking.
Ana laughs as she slides across the pond.

items.hint: Look for the person who checks for danger first.
items.explanation: Cautious means careful to avoid danger. Mila tests the ice before she trusts it.

wrong.b: Jon does not check at all, so he is careless, not cautious.
wrong.c: Ana is having fun, but nothing shows she is being careful.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Mom is ___ with hot pans, so she always uses thick oven mitts.
items.clue: always uses thick oven mitts
items.hint: Why would someone always wear thick mitts?
items.explanation: "Always uses thick oven mitts" shows Mom is careful not to get burned. That is cautious.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "cautious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The cautious hiker stayed far away from the edge of the cliff.
items.hint: The opposite of being careful about danger is...?
items.explanation: Reckless means not caring about danger, the opposite of cautious. Careful means the same as cautious, not the opposite.

wrong.a: Careful is a synonym of cautious, not its opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what cautious means.
items.hint: A cautious person is careful. Which ending shows care?
items.explanation: Taking small, slow steps on a wet floor is careful, so it shows caution. Running and sliding is careless.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Lily?
items.passage: Before she touched the strange plant, Lily put on gloves and asked her teacher if it was safe.
items.clue: put on gloves; asked her teacher if it was safe
items.hint: What does Lily do before she touches the plant?
items.explanation: Lily "put on gloves" and "asked if it was safe" before touching anything. Checking for danger first is being cautious.

words.definition: lucky; having something good happen to you

hero.text: Bolt was fortunate that the storm stopped just as he finished fixing the bridge.

words.everyday: We were fortunate to get a sunny day for our class picnic.

contrast.nonExample: Ella practiced every single day, so she earned a spot on the soccer team.
contrast.explanation: Fortunate means something good happens by luck. Ella earned her spot through hard work, so it was not just luck.

items.prompt: Is Max fortunate?
items.passage: Max dropped his ice cream cone, but it landed right side up on a clean plate.
items.hint: Did something lucky happen to Max?
items.explanation: Fortunate means lucky. The cone landing safely on a clean plate was a lucky break for Max.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Our bus was late, but we were ___ because the show had not started yet.
items.clue: the show had not started yet
items.hint: Being late could have been bad. What happened instead?
items.explanation: "The show had not started yet" means things worked out by luck even though the bus was late. That is fortunate.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "fortunate" in this sentence?
items.passage: Nia felt fortunate to find her lost key in the tall grass.
items.hint: Finding a tiny key in tall grass takes some luck.
items.explanation: Lucky means the same as fortunate. Clever would mean she found it by being smart, but the sentence is about good luck.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what fortunate means.

chunks.text: because he lost his lunch money

items.hint: Fortunate means something lucky happened. Which reason is lucky?
items.explanation: Finding a dollar is a lucky surprise, so Sam was fortunate. Losing money is unlucky.

items.prompt: The prefix un- means "not." What does "unfortunate" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: It was unfortunate that rain cancelled our baseball game.
items.hint: Un- + fortunate = not ___.
items.explanation: Un- means not, so unfortunate means not lucky. A cancelled game is bad luck.

wrong.a: Lucky is what fortunate means. The un- flips it to the opposite.

words.definition: wanting to know or learn about something

hero.text: Pixel was curious about the glowing rock, so she studied it under her magnifier.

words.everyday: The curious toddler opened every kitchen drawer to see what was inside.

contrast.nonExample: Leo yawned and looked away when his friend showed him the new fish tank.
contrast.explanation: Curious people want to find out more. Leo showed no interest at all, so he was bored, not curious.

items.prompt: What does "curious" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Jada was curious about how bees make honey.

options.text: afraid that something will hurt you

items.hint: Jada is wondering HOW bees do something.
items.explanation: Curious means wanting to know more. Jada wonders how bees make honey, so she wants to learn.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ puppy sniffed the new box to find out what was inside.
items.clue: to find out what was inside
items.hint: The puppy wants to find something out.
items.explanation: "To find out what was inside" shows the puppy wants to know something. That is curious.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "curious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The curious students asked the zookeeper many questions about the snakes.
items.hint: Curious students ask lots of questions. What kind of students would ask none?
items.explanation: Bored students don't care to learn more, the opposite of curious. Interested is a synonym, not an opposite.

wrong.a: Interested means almost the same as curious.

items.prompt: Which line uses "curious" correctly?

options.text: "I'm curious about what's in that box. Can we open it?"
"I'm so curious that I never want to know what is inside it."
"I felt curious, so I went right to sleep."

items.hint: A curious person wants to find out more.
items.explanation: Wanting to open the box to see what's inside shows curiosity. Not wanting to know, or going to sleep, shows no curiosity.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Omar?
items.passage: Omar kept asking questions about the moon and checked out five library books about space.
items.clue: kept asking questions; checked out five library books
items.hint: What do all those questions and books tell you about Omar?
items.explanation: "Kept asking questions" and "five library books about space" show Omar wants to learn more. That is curious.

words.definition: to say what you think will happen before it happens

hero.text: Kai looked at the dark clouds and predicted the storm would reach the city by noon.

words.everyday: Before reading the story, our class predicted that the fox would trick the hen.

contrast.nonExample: After the game was over, Ty told everyone the final score.
contrast.explanation: To predict, you tell what will happen BEFORE it happens. Ty reported the score after the game, so he did not predict it.

items.prompt: Which person is predicting?

options.text: Zara says, "I think the ice cube will melt in ten minutes."
Zara says, "The ice cube melted while we sat and watched it."
Zara says, "The ice cube feels cold and wet."

items.hint: Who talks about something that has not happened yet?
items.explanation: To predict is to say what will happen before it does. "Will melt" is about the future.

wrong.b: "Melted" already happened, so Zara is telling what she saw, not predicting.
wrong.c: Zara is describing how it feels right now.

items.prompt: The prefix pre- means "before," and dict means "say." What does "predict" mean?

options.text: to say something so loudly that all can hear
to say what will happen before it happens
to repeat what someone else just said
to write down every word very carefully

items.hint: Put the parts together: say + before.
items.explanation: Pre- (before) + dict (say) = to say before. When you predict, you say what will happen before it happens.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Can you ___ what will happen if we leave the ice cream in the sun?
items.clue: what will happen
items.hint: The question asks about something in the future.
items.explanation: "What will happen" asks you to think ahead. Saying what will happen before it does is predicting.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what predict means.

chunks.text: that the gray turtle would win.
that the gray turtle had already won.

items.hint: A prediction is about what WILL happen.
items.explanation: "Would win" talks about the future, which is a prediction. "Had already won" can't be true before the race even started.

items.prompt: Which word best names what the weather reporter did?
items.passage: The weather reporter studied the maps and told viewers that snow would fall tomorrow.
items.clue: would fall tomorrow
items.hint: Is the reporter talking about the past or the future?
items.explanation: "Would fall tomorrow" is about the future, so the reporter predicted. Recalled means remembered something from the past.

words.definition: wanting very much to do or have something

hero.text: Rex was eager to try his new jet boots and was the first one out the door.

words.everyday: The eager students raised their hands before the teacher even finished the question.

contrast.nonExample: Ben dragged his feet and walked as slowly as he could on the way to the dentist.
contrast.explanation: Eager means you really want to do something. Ben moved slowly because he did not want to go, so he was reluctant.

items.prompt: Is Lucy eager for the field trip?
items.passage: Lucy packed her bag the night before the field trip and woke up extra early.
items.hint: Does Lucy seem to really want to go?
items.explanation: Packing early and waking up early show Lucy really wants to go. That is eager.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The dog was ___ to go for a walk and waited by the door with its leash.
items.clue: waited by the door with its leash
items.hint: What does waiting by the door with a leash show?
items.explanation: "Waited by the door with its leash" shows the dog really wanted to go. That is eager.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "eager" in this sentence?
items.passage: Tom was eager to share his science project with the class.
items.hint: Look for a word that means NOT wanting to do it.
items.explanation: Reluctant means not wanting to, the opposite of eager. Excited and ready are close to eager.

wrong.b: Excited is close to eager, not opposite.
wrong.c: Ready is close to eager, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what eager means.

chunks.text: so she hid in her room.

items.hint: An eager person can't wait. Which ending shows that?
items.explanation: Sitting down early shows Maya couldn't wait to start. Hiding in her room shows she didn't want to go.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Jamal?
items.passage: Jamal couldn't wait to open his new paints and kept asking when he could start.
items.clue: couldn't wait; kept asking when he could start
items.hint: How does Jamal feel about starting?
items.explanation: "Couldn't wait" and "kept asking when he could start" show Jamal really wanted to paint. That is eager.

words.definition: shy and easily frightened; not brave

hero.text: The timid kitten hid behind Nova's boots until she spoke to it softly.

words.everyday: On the first day of school, the timid new boy spoke in a tiny whisper.

contrast.nonExample: Grace walked right up to the new students and introduced herself with a big smile.
contrast.explanation: Timid people are shy or easily scared. Grace was bold and friendly, the opposite of timid.

items.prompt: Which animal is timid?

options.text: A rabbit freezes and hides when a leaf falls nearby.
A big dog runs up and barks loudly at every person.
A cat stretches out in the warm sun.

items.hint: Which animal gets scared very easily?
items.explanation: Timid means easily frightened. The rabbit hides from something as small as a falling leaf.

wrong.b: The dog is bold and loud, the opposite of timid.
wrong.c: The cat is relaxed, not frightened.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ girl hid behind her mom when the clown said hello.
items.clue: hid behind her mom
items.hint: Why might a child hide when someone says hello?
items.explanation: "Hid behind her mom" shows the girl was shy and a little scared. That is timid.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "timid" in this sentence?
items.passage: The timid deer ran away at the smallest sound.
items.hint: Why would a deer run from a tiny sound?
items.explanation: Fearful means easily scared, like timid. The deer might be fast too, but running at the smallest sound shows fear.

wrong.c: The deer may be fast, but timid is about being easily scared, not speed.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what timid means.
items.hint: Timid people are shy. Which choice is shy?
items.explanation: Speaking softly around new people is shy, so it shows timid. Shouting hello to everyone is bold.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Ella?
items.passage: Ella wanted to join the game at recess, but she felt too shy and scared to ask.
items.clue: too shy and scared to ask
items.hint: What stops Ella from asking?
items.explanation: "Too shy and scared to ask" shows Ella is timid. She wants to play but feels afraid.

words.definition: to watch something carefully to learn about it

hero.text: Juniper observed the robot from the rooftop for an hour to learn how it moved.

words.everyday: In science class, we observed a caterpillar every day as it turned into a butterfly.

contrast.nonExample: Jake glanced at the clock for one second and kept running down the hall.
contrast.explanation: To observe is to watch carefully, often for a while, to learn something. A one-second look is not careful watching.

items.prompt: Is Rosa observing the birds?
items.passage: Rosa sat quietly by the bird feeder for twenty minutes, writing down which birds came.
items.hint: Is Rosa watching carefully to learn something?
items.explanation: Rosa watches closely for a long time and writes down what she sees. That is observing.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Scientists ___ the frogs closely to learn what they eat.
items.clue: closely; to learn
items.hint: How do scientists learn about animals?
items.explanation: "Closely" and "to learn" show careful watching. That is observing.

wrong.b: Imitate means copy. Scientists learn by watching the frogs, not copying them.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "observe" in this sentence?
items.passage: Please observe how the colors mix when I add water to the paint.
items.hint: What should you do with your eyes while the colors mix?
items.explanation: Watch is closest to observe here. Ignore is the opposite, and guess means you don't look at all.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what observe means.

chunks.text: and drew how its shape changed.
without ever looking up at it.

items.hint: Observing means looking carefully. Which ending fits?
items.explanation: Drawing how the moon's shape changed shows careful watching. You can't observe something without looking at it.

items.prompt: Which line uses "observe" correctly?

options.text: "I will observe the ball by kicking it into the goal."
"Let's observe the ants and see where they go."
"Keep your eyes shut tight while you observe the picture on the wall."

items.hint: Observing means watching carefully.
items.explanation: Watching the ants to see where they go is observing. Kicking is not watching, and you can't observe with your eyes shut.

words.definition: to tell what something is like using words

hero.text: Pixel described the missing dog to Bolt: small, brown, with one white ear.

words.everyday: Can you describe your favorite meal so well that I can almost taste it?

contrast.nonExample: Mia pointed at the puppy without saying a word.
contrast.explanation: To describe is to use words to tell what something is like. Pointing shows where it is but gives no details.

items.prompt: Which person is describing something?

options.text: Ivy says her kite is red and diamond-shaped, with a long tail.
Ivy runs across the field and flies her kite high in the windy sky.
Ivy buys a kite at the store.

items.hint: Who uses words to tell what something looks like?
items.explanation: Describing means telling what something is like. Ivy tells the kite's color, shape, and tail.

wrong.b: Ivy is flying the kite, not telling what it is like.
wrong.c: Buying a kite is not using words to tell about it.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Use three adjectives to ___ the ocean in your poem.
items.clue: three adjectives; poem
items.hint: Adjectives are describing words.
items.explanation: Adjectives tell what something is like, so you use them to describe the ocean.

items.prompt: Which words are closest in meaning to "describe" in this sentence?
items.passage: Will you describe the house where you grew up?
items.hint: The person is asking you to use words.
items.explanation: To describe the house is to tell about it in words: its rooms, colors, and yard.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what describe means.

chunks.text: about the loud thunder and bright flashes.
nothing at all on her paper.

items.hint: Describing uses details. Which ending gives details?
items.explanation: Writing about the loud thunder and bright flashes tells what the storm was like. Writing nothing describes nothing.

items.prompt: What is the officer asking the person to do?
items.passage: The officer asked, "What did the thief look like? Tell me his height, hair, and clothes."
items.clue: What did the thief look like? Tell me
items.hint: The officer wants to know what the thief was like.
items.explanation: "What did the thief look like? Tell me..." asks the person to use words to tell details. That is describing.

words.definition: to look at how two or more things are alike and different

hero.text: Kai compared the two footprints in the mud and saw that one was much bigger.

words.everyday: In math, we compared the two numbers to see which one was greater.

contrast.nonExample: Lily looked at one apple and said it was red.
contrast.explanation: Comparing needs at least two things. Lily only described one apple, so she did not compare.

items.prompt: Is Jack comparing?
items.passage: Jack held up one leaf and counted the points around its edge.
items.hint: How many leaves is Jack looking at?
items.explanation: To compare, you need two or more things. Jack studies only one leaf, so he is not comparing.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Let's ___ the two maps to see which road is shorter.
items.clue: the two maps; which road is shorter
items.hint: You are looking at two things to find a difference.
items.explanation: "The two maps" and "which road is shorter" mean looking at how they differ. That is comparing.

items.prompt: What does "compared" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The coach compared the two runners' times.

options.text: cheered loudly for each runner in the race
wrote down each time on a chart
looked at how the times were alike or different

items.hint: What do you do with two things when you compare them?
items.explanation: Comparing means looking at how things are alike and different, like which runner was faster.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what compare means.

chunks.text: she saw that one had more chips.
she looked at only one of them.

items.hint: Comparing means finding a difference or sameness between things.
items.explanation: Seeing that one cookie had more chips is a difference found by comparing. Looking at only one cookie is not comparing.

items.prompt: Which word best tells what Ben did?
items.passage: Ben made a chart showing how frogs and toads are the same and how they are different.
items.clue: how they are the same and how they are different
items.hint: Ben looks at two animals side by side.
items.explanation: "The same" and "different" are the two parts of comparing. Ben compared frogs and toads.

words.definition: very, very old; from a long, long time ago

hero.text: Rex found an ancient map in the museum that was thousands of years old.

words.everyday: Ancient Egyptians built the pyramids more than four thousand years ago.

contrast.nonExample: Dad's car is ten years old and has a few scratches.
contrast.explanation: Ancient means extremely old, often thousands of years. Ten years is old for a car, but it is not ancient.

items.prompt: Which thing is ancient?

options.text: a clay pot made 3,000 years ago

items.hint: Which one is from the longest time ago?
items.explanation: Ancient means very, very old. A pot from 3,000 years ago is ancient.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ castle was built more than a thousand years ago.
items.clue: more than a thousand years ago
items.hint: Look at how long ago the castle was built.
items.explanation: "More than a thousand years ago" tells you the castle is extremely old. That is ancient.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "ancient" in this sentence?
items.passage: Scientists studied the ancient bones of a dinosaur.
items.hint: Ancient is about age. Which word is about age?
items.explanation: Ancient means very old, so new is the opposite. Huge, broken, and heavy describe size or condition, not age.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what ancient means.
items.hint: Ancient things are very, very old.
items.explanation: Two thousand years makes the tree ancient. A tree that started growing last spring is young.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the coin?
items.passage: Ms. Lee showed us a coin from Rome that people used about 2,000 years ago.
items.clue: about 2,000 years ago
items.hint: How old is the coin?
items.explanation: "About 2,000 years ago" shows the coin is extremely old, so it is ancient.

words.definition: easily broken or damaged

hero.text: Nova carried the fragile glass statue with both hands so it would not crack.

words.everyday: The box said FRAGILE, so we carried the dishes inside very carefully.

contrast.nonExample: Sam's rubber ball bounced off the brick wall without a single scratch.
contrast.explanation: Fragile things break easily. The rubber ball is tough and bouncy, so it is sturdy, not fragile.

items.prompt: Is the egg fragile?
items.passage: A bird's egg can crack if you squeeze it even a little.
items.hint: Does the egg break easily?
items.explanation: Fragile means easily broken. An egg that cracks with a small squeeze is fragile.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Be gentle with the butterfly, because its thin wings are very ___.
items.clue: Be gentle; thin wings
items.hint: Why do you need to be gentle with thin wings?
items.explanation: "Be gentle" and "thin wings" show the wings could tear easily. That is fragile.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "fragile" in this sentence?
items.passage: The old book had fragile pages that tore when you touched them.
items.hint: The pages tore when touched.
items.explanation: Delicate means easily damaged, like fragile. Pages that tear at a touch are delicate.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what fragile means.

chunks.text: so we could kick it around.

items.hint: Fragile things need protection.
items.explanation: You wrap a fragile vase so it won't break. Kicking a fragile vase would smash it.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the teacups?
items.passage: Grandma's teacups are so thin that even a small bump could chip them.
items.clue: so thin; even a small bump could chip them
items.hint: What could happen with just a small bump?
items.explanation: "Even a small bump could chip them" shows the cups break easily. That is fragile. Sturdy is the opposite.

words.definition: happy to give or share, often more than you have to

hero.text: Bolt was generous and gave half of his snack to a hungry kid in the park.

words.everyday: Our generous neighbor shares tomatoes from her garden with the whole street.

contrast.nonExample: Ollie kept all the crayons in a pile and would not let anyone use them.
contrast.explanation: Generous people share and give freely. Ollie kept everything for himself, so he was selfish.

items.prompt: Which person is generous?

options.text: Ruby keeps every cookie for herself and hides the jar.
Ruby shares her cookies with the whole class.
Ruby counts her cookies and eats one.

items.hint: Who gives to others?
items.explanation: Generous means happy to give and share. Ruby shares with the whole class.

wrong.a: Hiding the jar is selfish, the opposite of generous.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: It was ___ of Marco to give his old bike to his little cousin.
items.clue: give his old bike to his little cousin
items.hint: What kind of person gives away a bike?
items.explanation: Giving his bike to his cousin is a kind act of giving. That is generous.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "generous" in this sentence?
items.passage: The generous baker gave free bread to everyone in line.
items.hint: Which person would NOT give bread away?
items.explanation: Selfish people keep things for themselves, the opposite of generous people who give.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what generous means.

chunks.text: his umbrella with a friend in the rain.
nothing and kept his umbrella to himself.

items.hint: Generous people share.
items.explanation: Sharing his umbrella is generous. Keeping it to himself is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Mia?
items.passage: Mia gave away ten of her twelve toys to children who had none.
items.clue: gave away ten of her twelve toys
items.hint: Mia is not just using good manners. What is she doing?
items.explanation: Giving away most of her toys is giving freely, which is generous. Polite is about good manners, like saying please, not about giving.

wrong.a: Polite means having good manners. Mia is giving a lot away, which is generous.

words.definition: to look at something quickly

hero.text: Pixel glanced at her watch and saw she had one minute to reach the bank.

words.everyday: During the test, Ana glanced at the clock and then went back to work.

contrast.nonExample: Owen stared at the painting for ten minutes, studying every color.
contrast.explanation: A glance is quick. Owen looked for a long time, so he stared or studied it.

items.prompt: Did Ken glance at the map?
items.passage: Ken looked at the map for a long time, tracing every road with his finger.
items.hint: Was Ken's look quick or long?
items.explanation: To glance is to look quickly. Ken looked for a long time, so he studied the map instead.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Before crossing the street, Ava ___ quickly to the left and right.
items.clue: quickly to the left and right
items.hint: What do you do with your eyes before crossing?
items.explanation: "Quickly" and "left and right" show Ava took fast looks. That is glancing.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "glanced" in this sentence?
items.passage: Dad glanced at the newspaper headline before running out the door.
items.hint: A glance is short. What is a long look called?
items.explanation: Stared means looked for a long time, the opposite of a quick glance. Peeked is close in meaning to glanced.

wrong.a: Peeked is a quick look too, so it is close in meaning, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what glance means.

chunks.text: for just a second before she ordered.
for a whole hour before she ordered.

items.hint: A glance is very short.
items.explanation: A glance lasts about a second. Looking for a whole hour is not a glance.

items.prompt: Which word best tells what the goalie did?
items.passage: The goalie took one quick look over her shoulder just before the ball came.
items.clue: one quick look
items.hint: Was her look long and careful, or fast?
items.explanation: "One quick look" is a glance. Observed would mean watching carefully for a while.

wrong.a: Observing is careful watching over time. The goalie only took one quick look.

words.definition: happening slowly, a little at a time

hero.text: Juniper's power made a gradual glow that grew brighter, little by little, until the cave was lit.

words.everyday: The gradual change of the leaves from green to red took several weeks.

contrast.nonExample: All the lights in the house went off at once when the power failed.
contrast.explanation: Gradual changes happen slowly, step by step. The lights went off all at once, so the change was sudden.

items.prompt: What does "gradual" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: There was a gradual rise in the river after days of light rain.

options.text: sudden and very fast, all at once
slow, a little at a time

items.hint: Light rain for days would make the river rise how?
items.explanation: Gradual means slow and a little at a time. Days of light rain raised the river slowly.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The puppy's growth was ___, so we never noticed it getting bigger each day.
items.clue: never noticed it getting bigger each day
items.hint: Why wouldn't you notice a change each day?
items.explanation: You don't notice a change each day when it happens slowly, a little at a time. That is gradual.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "gradual" in this sentence?
items.passage: The hill had a gradual slope that was easy to walk up.
items.hint: A gradual slope rises slowly. What kind of slope rises sharply?
items.explanation: A gradual slope goes up a little at a time. A steep slope goes up sharply, the opposite. Gentle means almost the same as gradual here.

wrong.a: Gentle is close in meaning to gradual for a hill, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what gradual means.

chunks.text: getting a little taller each week.

items.hint: Gradual means little by little.
items.explanation: Growing a little each week is gradual. Shooting up overnight is sudden.

items.prompt: Is this a gradual change?

contrast.explanation: A habitat is the natural place where a plant or animal lives and finds what it needs. A store is a place people visit to shop, not a natural home.

the bus that takes us to school

items.explanation: A habitat is the natural place an animal lives. The desert is a camel's habitat.

items.passage: Monkeys live high in the trees of the rainforest, where they find fruit and stay safe.

words.definition: to copy the way someone looks, acts, or sounds

contrast.nonExample: Zoe made up a brand-new dance that nobody had ever seen before.
contrast.explanation: To imitate is to copy someone else. Zoe created something new, so she was inventing, not imitating.

items.explanation: To imitate is to copy. The parrot copies its owner's voice.

items.explanation: The baby tries to make the same sounds as her father. Copying sounds is imitating.

"Please imitate the box onto the top shelf."

words.definition: wild and rushed because of fear or worry

hero.text: Bolt made a frantic search for the lost child as the crowd grew bigger.

words.everyday: Mom was frantic when she couldn't find her car keys and we were already late.

contrast.nonExample: Jen calmly packed her bag for the trip while humming a song.
contrast.explanation: Frantic means rushed and worried. Jen was calm and relaxed, so she was not frantic.

items.prompt: Which person is frantic?

options.text: Ray sits on a soft blanket and reads quietly under a shady tree.
Ray runs around yelling, "Where is my dog? I can't find him!"

items.hint: Who is rushing around in a worried way?
items.explanation: Frantic means wild and rushed with worry. Ray runs and yells because he can't find his dog.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: When the bees flew into the tent, the ___ campers ran around waving their arms.
items.clue: ran around waving their arms
items.hint: How do people act when bees surprise them?
items.explanation: "Ran around waving their arms" shows wild, scared rushing. That is frantic.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "frantic" in this sentence?
items.passage: We made a frantic dash to the bus stop before the bus pulled away.
items.hint: Frantic is wild and worried. What is the opposite feeling?
items.explanation: Calm is relaxed and steady, the opposite of frantic. Quick describes speed, and a frantic dash is quick too.

wrong.a: A frantic dash is quick, so quick is not the opposite.

items.hint: Frantic animals rush around in fear.
items.explanation: Dashing under the bed is a scared, rushed action, so it shows frantic. A peaceful nap is calm.

items.passage: Late for the bus, Ava ran around the kitchen grabbing papers and dropping her pencil.
items.clue: Late; ran around grabbing papers and dropping her pencil
items.hint: How is Ava moving, and why?
items.explanation: Being late and running around grabbing and dropping things shows wild, worried rushing. That is frantic.

words.definition: extremely angry

hero.text: Nova was furious when the thief smashed the museum window, and her eyes blazed.

words.everyday: Dad was furious when someone dumped trash all over our clean yard.

contrast.nonExample: Jo frowned a little when the tip of her pencil broke.
contrast.explanation: Furious means very, very angry. A small frown over a broken pencil is only a little annoyed.

items.prompt: What does "furious" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The farmer was furious when the goats ate his whole garden.
items.hint: How would you feel if goats ate your WHOLE garden?
items.explanation: Furious means extremely angry. Losing the whole garden would make the farmer very angry.

items.passage: Kim was ___ when her little brother broke her new tablet on purpose.

items.hint: How would someone feel if their new thing was broken on purpose?
items.explanation: Breaking something new "on purpose" would make Kim extremely angry. That is furious.

items.hint: Is Kai a little angry or extremely angry?
items.explanation: A red face and yelling as loud as he could show extreme anger, so furious fits. Annoyed is only a little angry, which is too weak here.

wrong.a: Annoyed means a little bothered. Kai's red face and loud yelling show much stronger anger.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what furious means.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "furious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The furious bull snorted and charged at the fence.
items.hint: Snorting and charging show a strong feeling.
items.explanation: Enraged means filled with rage, or extremely angry, just like furious. Gentle is the opposite.

words.definition: feeling thankful for something someone did or gave

words.everyday: I was grateful when my friend helped me carry my heavy backpack home.

contrast.nonExample: Liam got a new sweater as a gift and complained that it was the wrong color.
contrast.explanation: Grateful people feel and show thanks. Liam complained instead of being thankful.

items.prompt: Is Ana grateful?
items.passage: After Ms. Park helped Ana with her reading, Ana made her a thank-you card.

items.explanation: The firefighters saved a home, so people would feel thankful to them. That is grateful.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "grateful" in this sentence?
items.passage: The tired hikers were grateful for the cool water.

items.explanation: Thankful means the same as grateful. The hikers were thankful for the water.

words.definition: normal and usual; not special or different

hero.text: Pixel looked like an ordinary student at her desk, but she was secretly a hero.

words.everyday: It was an ordinary Tuesday: breakfast, school, homework, and bed.

contrast.nonExample: On parade day, a giant balloon dragon floated down Main Street.
contrast.explanation: Ordinary means plain and usual. A giant balloon dragon is special and unusual, not ordinary.

a sparrow hopping on the sidewalk

items.explanation: Ordinary means normal and usual. A sparrow on the sidewalk is something you see every day.

items.hint: "But" shows a surprise. The inside was special, so the outside was...?
items.explanation: "But" sets up a contrast with the special crystals inside. The outside was plain and normal, or ordinary.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "ordinary" in this sentence?

items.explanation: Unusual means not normal, the opposite of ordinary. Usual means the same as ordinary.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what ordinary means.

items.explanation: "Just" and "like every other weekend" show the party was normal and usual. That is ordinary. Peculiar means strange, the opposite.

words.definition: very happy and pleased

words.everyday: Grandma was delighted when we surprised her with flowers on her birthday.

contrast.nonExample: Ian felt just okay about getting a plain pencil as a prize.
contrast.explanation: Delighted means very happy. Feeling just okay is not strong enough to be delighted.

items.prompt: Is Jada delighted?

items.hint: How happy does Jada seem?

words.definition: a little angry or bothered

words.everyday: I get annoyed when my sister hums the same song over and over.

contrast.nonExample: Pia screamed and threw her backpack when her brother smashed her model ship.
contrast.explanation: Annoyed means only a little angry. Screaming and throwing things show someone is furious, which is much stronger.

words.definition: able to wait calmly without getting upset

items.hint: Are there enough tickets for everyone?
items.explanation: "Only three" tickets for "hundreds of people" means there were very few. That is scarce. Plentiful is the opposite.

words.definition: showing good sense; wise and practical

words.everyday: Wearing warm boots in the snow is a sensible choice.

contrast.explanation: Sensible choices are wise and practical. Flip-flops on a rocky trail are an unwise choice.

taking an umbrella on a rainy day

items.hint: Is getting ready before a storm wise?
items.explanation: Getting water and a flashlight ready "before the storm" is wise and practical. That is sensible.

words.everyday: A rubber band is flexible, so you can stretch it and it snaps back.

contrast.explanation: Flexible things bend without breaking. The dry stick broke, so it was stiff, not flexible.

items.prompt: Is the ruler flexible?
items.passage: Mia bent her plastic ruler into a curve, and it sprang back without breaking.
items.hint: Did the ruler bend without breaking?
items.explanation: Flexible means able to bend without breaking. The ruler curved and sprang back.

items.explanation: "Bend over" and "easily" show the gymnasts' bodies bend well. That is flexible.

items.explanation: Stiff means hard to bend, the opposite of flexible.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what flexible means.

items.prompt: What does "recall" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: I can recall every word of my favorite poem.

items.prompt: Which words are closest in meaning to "rely on" in this sentence?
items.passage: You can rely on Tia to keep a secret.
items.hint: Can you trust Tia with a secret?
items.explanation: Count on means trust and depend on, the same as rely on. You can trust Tia to keep a secret.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what rely means.

chunks.text: We rely on our bus driver

items.hint: You rely on people you can trust.
items.explanation: Being on time every day makes the driver someone you can trust, so we rely on her. You can't rely on someone who is always late.

items.prompt: Which sentence tells about the farmer and his tractor?
items.passage: The farmer needs his tractor every single day to plow his fields.
items.clue: needs his tractor every single day
items.hint: What does needing something every day tell you?
items.explanation: "Needs his tractor every single day" shows the farmer depends on it. That is relying on it.

words.definition: worried or a little scared about what might happen

hero.text: Kai felt nervous before his first big rescue, and his hands shook a little.

words.everyday: Ella was nervous before her piano recital, so she took slow, deep breaths.

contrast.nonExample: Ty smiled and strolled onto the stage, relaxed, for his tenth show.
contrast.explanation: Nervous means worried or jumpy about what might happen. Ty was calm and relaxed, so he was not nervous.

items.prompt: Which person is nervous?

options.text: Ben bites his nails, and his tummy flips before the spelling bee.
Ben naps happily on the couch.
Ben eats a big turkey sandwich with chips at the lunch table.

items.hint: Who is worried about something that is about to happen?
items.explanation: Nervous means worried about what might happen. Biting nails and a flipping tummy before the spelling bee show worry.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Olivia felt ___ while she waited for the doctor to give her a shot.
items.clue: waited for the doctor to give her a shot
items.hint: How do many kids feel waiting for a shot?
items.explanation: Waiting for a shot makes many people worried about what will happen. That is nervous.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "nervous" in this sentence?
items.passage: The nervous cat jumped at every little noise.
items.hint: The cat jumped at every noise.
items.explanation: Jumpy means easily startled and on edge, close to nervous. "Jumped at every little noise" is the clue.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what nervous means.

chunks.text: so he studied extra the night before.
so he didn't think about it at all.

items.hint: Nervous people worry about what is coming.
items.explanation: Worrying about the test made Lucas study extra, which fits nervous. Not thinking about it at all shows no worry.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Zoe?
items.passage: Before her first swim race, Zoe's heart pounded and she kept worrying she would come in last.
items.clue: heart pounded; kept worrying
items.hint: Is Zoe happy, angry, or worried?
items.explanation: A pounding heart and "kept worrying" before the race show Zoe was nervous. A pounding heart can come with anger too, but she is worried, not angry.

words.definition: honest and truly meaning what you say

hero.text: Juniper gave a sincere apology to the baker after she crashed into his shop.

words.everyday: Luis wrote a sincere note telling his teacher how much her help meant to him.

contrast.nonExample: Rita told Jo, "I love your hat!" and then whispered to a friend that it looked silly.
contrast.explanation: Sincere means you really mean what you say. Rita said one thing but meant another, so she was not sincere.

items.prompt: Was Ali's apology sincere?
items.passage: Ali said sorry only because the teacher made him, and he rolled his eyes as he said it.
items.hint: Did Ali really mean his sorry?
items.explanation: Sincere means truly meaning what you say. Rolling his eyes and only saying sorry because he had to show Ali did not mean it.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Her warm, ___ smile showed she was truly happy to see us.
items.clue: truly happy
items.hint: Her smile was real, not fake.
items.explanation: "Truly happy" shows the smile was real and honest. That is sincere.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "sincere" in this sentence?
items.passage: Mom gave a sincere thank-you to the nurse who helped us.
items.hint: Sincere means real and honest. What is the opposite?
items.explanation: Fake means not real or not meant, the opposite of sincere.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what sincere means.

chunks.text: to fix the fence he broke.
and then laughed that he didn't mean it.

items.hint: A sincere apology is really meant.
items.explanation: Promising to fix the fence shows Tom truly means his apology. Laughing that he didn't mean it makes it not sincere.

items.prompt: Which line sounds sincere?

options.text: "Fine, I'm sorry, okay? Can we please stop talking about your silly old toy now?"
"I'm really sorry I broke your toy. I'll save up to buy you a new one."

items.hint: Which speaker truly means it?
items.explanation: Saying "really sorry" and offering to replace the toy shows the speaker truly means it. That is sincere. The other lines sound annoyed or careless.

words.definition: lasting for only a short time

hero.text: Rex built a temporary bridge so people could cross until the real one was fixed.

words.everyday: The tattoo from the fair was temporary and washed off in the bath.

contrast.nonExample: The old stone wall has stood around the farm for two hundred years.
contrast.explanation: Temporary things last only a short time. The wall has lasted for centuries, so it is permanent.

items.prompt: Which thing is temporary?

options.text: a mountain that has stood for millions of years
a sandcastle that the tide washes away
a brick school built to last a hundred years

items.hint: Which one lasts only a short time?
items.explanation: Temporary means lasting only a short time. A sandcastle washes away the same day.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: While the roof was fixed, the gym became our ___ classroom for two weeks.
items.clue: While the roof was fixed; for two weeks
items.hint: How long would they use the gym?
items.explanation: "While the roof was fixed" and "for two weeks" show the gym was used for only a short time. That is temporary.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "temporary" in this sentence?
items.passage: The road is closed, but it is only a temporary problem.
items.hint: Which word means lasting forever?
items.explanation: Permanent means lasting for a very long time or forever, the opposite of temporary.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what temporary means.

chunks.text: to take it off in two days.
to wear it for the rest of my life.

items.hint: Temporary things don't last long.
items.explanation: Taking the bandage off in two days fits temporary. Wearing it forever would be permanent.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the shop?
items.passage: The pop-up shop sold ice cream on the beach for one week, and then it closed.
items.clue: for one week, and then it closed
items.hint: How long was the shop open?
items.explanation: "For one week, and then it closed" shows the shop lasted a short time. That is temporary.

words.definition: to disappear suddenly or completely

hero.text: Pixel vanished in a flash of light and appeared on the other side of the street.

words.everyday: The cookies vanished from the plate in just five minutes.

contrast.nonExample: The puppy hid under the blanket, but we could see its tail sticking out.
contrast.explanation: To vanish is to disappear completely. We could still see the puppy's tail, so it had not vanished.

items.prompt: Did the fog vanish?
items.passage: The sun came out, and in a few minutes the thick fog was completely gone.
items.hint: Was the fog still there?
items.explanation: To vanish is to disappear completely. The fog was "completely gone," so it vanished.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: When the hot sun came out, the puddles began to ___.
items.clue: the hot sun came out
items.hint: What happens to puddles in hot sun?
items.explanation: The hot sun dries puddles until they are gone. They vanish.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "vanish" in this sentence?
items.passage: The magician made the coin vanish from his open hand.
items.hint: What is a magician's coin trick?
items.explanation: Disappear means the same as vanish. The coin is suddenly gone from his hand.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what vanish means.

chunks.text: so fast that no one saw where it went.
and stayed right where we could see it.

items.hint: When something vanishes, you can't see it anymore.
items.explanation: No one saw where the rabbit went, so it vanished. Staying where we could see it is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word best tells what the deer did?
items.passage: One second the deer was standing in the field, and the next second it was gone.
items.clue: the next second it was gone
items.hint: Where was the deer a second later?
items.explanation: "The next second it was gone" shows the deer disappeared suddenly. That is vanished.

words.definition: having a lot of money or valuable things

hero.text: A wealthy store owner paid to rebuild the park that Bolt had saved.

words.everyday: The wealthy family owned three houses and a big sailboat.

contrast.nonExample: Sam saved his allowance for months to buy one new book.
contrast.explanation: Wealthy means having a lot of money. Sam had to save for months for one book, so he is not wealthy.

items.prompt: Which person is wealthy?

options.text: Mr. Gold has to count every last coin to buy one bus ticket.
Mr. Gold borrows money to pay for lunch.
Mr. Gold owns a mansion, ten cars, and a private jet.

items.hint: Who has a lot of money and valuable things?
items.explanation: Wealthy means having lots of money or valuable things. A mansion, ten cars, and a jet show great wealth.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ king had rooms filled with gold and jewels.
items.clue: rooms filled with gold and jewels
items.hint: What do rooms of gold tell you about the king?
items.explanation: "Rooms filled with gold and jewels" show the king had a lot of valuable things. That is wealthy.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "wealthy" in this sentence?
items.passage: The wealthy man bought the most expensive car in the shop.
items.hint: Wealthy is about money. What is the opposite?
items.explanation: Poor means having very little money, the opposite of wealthy. Rich is a synonym.

wrong.a: Rich means the same as wealthy, not the opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what wealthy means.

chunks.text: gave a million dollars to the hospital.
could not pay for a loaf of bread.

items.hint: Wealthy people have a lot of money.
items.explanation: Only someone with lots of money could give a million dollars. Not affording bread shows the opposite of wealthy.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the family?
items.passage: The family owns a huge house with a pool and travels around the world every summer.
items.clue: huge house with a pool; travels around the world every summer
items.hint: What does all of this cost?
items.explanation: A huge house, a pool, and trips around the world cost a lot of money, so the family is wealthy.

words.definition: (of a plant) to droop and go limp, often from heat or too little water

hero.text: Juniper sprayed water on the garden so the flowers would not wilt in the heat.

words.everyday: If you forget to water the basil, its leaves will wilt and hang down.

contrast.nonExample: After the rain, the tulips stood tall and bright in the garden.
contrast.explanation: When plants wilt, they droop and go limp. These tulips stood tall, so they did not wilt.

items.prompt: Did the lettuce wilt?
items.passage: The lettuce sat in the hot car all day, and its leaves became soft and floppy.
items.hint: What happened to the leaves in the heat?
items.explanation: To wilt is to droop and go limp. The lettuce leaves became soft and floppy in the heat.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: After a week with no water, the roses began to ___.
items.clue: a week with no water
items.hint: What happens to flowers without water?
items.explanation: Plants without water droop and go limp. "A week with no water" makes the roses wilt.

items.prompt: What does "wilted" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The flowers wilted in the hot afternoon sun.
items.hint: What does hot sun do to flowers?
items.explanation: Wilted means drooped and went limp. Hot sun dries flowers out so they hang down.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what wilt means.

chunks.text: after a week with no water,

items.hint: Wilted flowers droop.
items.explanation: Heads hanging low shows the daisies drooped, which is wilting. Standing straight is the opposite.

items.prompt: What happened to the pepper plants?
items.passage: Grandpa forgot to water his pepper plants in the heat wave. Their leaves hung down like wet paper.
items.clue: forgot to water; heat wave; leaves hung down
items.hint: Heat and no water make leaves do what?
items.explanation: No water, a heat wave, and leaves hanging down all show the plants drooped. They wilted. They did not vanish, because they were still there.

words.definition: strange or unusual

hero.text: Kai noticed a peculiar green glow coming from the empty lab late at night.

words.everyday: The milk had a peculiar smell, so we poured it down the sink.

contrast.nonExample: Our cat ate her food, napped in the sun, and purred, just like every day.
contrast.explanation: Peculiar means strange or unusual. The cat did what she does every day, which is ordinary.

items.prompt: Which is peculiar?

options.text: a dog that barks at the door
a dog that chews a bone
a dog that meows like a cat

items.hint: Which one is strange?
items.explanation: Peculiar means strange or unusual. Dogs don't usually meow, so that is peculiar.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The sound coming from the empty attic was ___, like someone humming and tapping a spoon.
items.clue: empty attic; like someone humming and tapping
items.hint: Is humming in an empty attic normal?
items.explanation: Humming and tapping in an attic is strange and unexpected. That is peculiar.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "peculiar" in this sentence?
items.passage: Ian wore a peculiar hat shaped like a fish.
items.hint: Is a fish-shaped hat normal?
items.explanation: Strange means the same as peculiar. A hat shaped like a fish is unusual. Boring is nearly the opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what peculiar means.

chunks.text: if someone had added something strange.
for another bowl of the same old soup.

items.hint: Peculiar means strange. Which ending fits?
items.explanation: A peculiar taste makes Mia wonder about something strange in it. "The same old soup" means nothing was unusual.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the tree?
items.passage: The tree in Ana's yard grows purple apples that taste like lemons.
items.clue: purple apples that taste like lemons
items.hint: Have you ever seen apples like that?
items.explanation: Purple apples that taste like lemons are very unusual, so the tree is peculiar. Ordinary means normal, the opposite.

wrong.a: Ordinary means normal. Purple lemon-flavored apples are not normal at all.

words.definition: a story people pass around that may not be true

hero.text: Bolt heard a rumor that a monster lived in the lake, so he went to check.

words.everyday: There was a rumor that school would close for snow, but it turned out to be false.

contrast.nonExample: The principal announced on the loudspeaker that the field trip is on Friday.
contrast.explanation: A rumor is passed from person to person and may not be true. This news came straight from the principal, so it is an official fact.

items.prompt: What is a rumor?
items.passage: A rumor spread that our teacher was moving to France.

options.text: a fact that a book has proven to be true
a story passed around that may not be true
a happy song that people sing together at school
a secret that only one single person knows

items.hint: The story "spread" from person to person.
items.explanation: A rumor is a story people pass around that may not be true. "Spread" shows it went from person to person.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The ___ about free ice cream spread fast, but no one knew if it was true.
items.clue: spread fast; no one knew if it was true
items.hint: What kind of story spreads but might not be true?
items.explanation: "Spread fast" and "no one knew if it was true" describe a rumor.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "rumor" in this sentence?
items.passage: Don't believe every rumor you hear on the playground.
items.hint: What kind of talk shouldn't you always believe?
items.explanation: Gossip is talk passed around about others that may not be true, like a rumor. A fact is proven true, which is the opposite.

wrong.c: A fact is known to be true. A rumor may not be true.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what rumor means.

chunks.text: a famous singer was visiting our school,
but nobody knew if it was true.
and everyone knew it was a proven fact.

items.hint: A rumor may or may not be true.
items.explanation: Rumors are stories no one is sure about. A "proven fact" is not a rumor.

items.prompt: Is this a rumor?
items.passage: Lena heard from a friend, who heard it from a cousin, that the town pool is closing forever.
items.hint: Where did the news come from? Is it sure to be true?
items.explanation: The story was passed from person to person, and no one official said it. That makes it a rumor.

words.definition: moving in an awkward way that makes you trip, bump, or drop things

hero.text: Rex was clumsy in his heavy new armor and tripped over the curb twice.

words.everyday: The clumsy puppy kept tripping over its own big paws.

contrast.nonExample: The dancer leaped and landed smoothly on her toes without a wobble.
contrast.explanation: Clumsy means awkward and likely to trip or drop things. The dancer moved smoothly and gracefully.

items.prompt: Is Tim being clumsy?
items.passage: In one morning, Tim knocked over his milk, dropped his spoon, and tripped on his backpack.
items.hint: Is Tim moving smoothly or awkwardly?
items.explanation: Clumsy means awkward and likely to trip or drop things. Tim spills, drops, and trips.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: I am so ___ today that I have dropped my pencil four times!
items.clue: dropped my pencil four times
items.hint: What kind of person keeps dropping things?
items.explanation: Dropping a pencil "four times" is awkward and careless. That is clumsy.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "clumsy" in this sentence?
items.passage: The clumsy waiter spilled soup all over the table.
items.hint: What do you call someone who moves smoothly and carefully?
items.explanation: Graceful means moving smoothly and easily, the opposite of clumsy.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what clumsy means.

chunks.text: bumped into the door and dropped his books.
walked across the balance beam without a wobble.

items.hint: Clumsy people bump and drop things.
items.explanation: Bumping and dropping things are clumsy. Walking a beam without a wobble is graceful.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Nora?
items.passage: Every time Nora carries a tray, she wobbles, trips, and spills something.
items.clue: wobbles, trips, and spills
items.hint: How does Nora move?
items.explanation: "Wobbles, trips, and spills" shows awkward moving. That is clumsy. Steady is the opposite.

words.definition: firm and not shaking or wobbling

hero.text: Nova held the ladder steady while the firefighter climbed up to the window.

words.everyday: Hold the camera steady, or the picture will come out blurry.

contrast.nonExample: The old table wobbles every time someone leans on it.
contrast.explanation: Steady means firm and not shaking. The wobbly table moves around, so it is not steady.

items.prompt: Which thing is steady?

options.text: a chair with one short leg that rocks
a ladder that stays still as you climb
a jelly that wiggles on the plate

items.hint: Which one does not shake or wobble?
items.explanation: Steady means firm and not wobbling. A ladder that stays still is steady.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Keep your hand ___ so the paint stays right on the line.
items.clue: so the paint stays right on the line
items.hint: What kind of hand paints a neat line?
items.explanation: To paint right on the line, your hand must not shake. That is steady. A clumsy or nervous hand might wobble.

wrong.b: A clumsy hand would make mistakes, not keep the paint on the line.
wrong.d: A nervous hand might shake, which is the opposite of what you need.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "steady" in this sentence?
items.passage: The doctor had steady hands as she stitched the cut.
items.hint: Steady hands don't move around. What do you call hands that do?
items.explanation: Shaky means trembling, the opposite of steady.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what steady means.

chunks.text: by sitting still in the middle,
so nobody fell into the lake.
so it rocked and tipped over.

items.hint: A steady boat doesn't rock.
items.explanation: Keeping the canoe steady means it doesn't rock, so nobody falls in. Rocking and tipping is the opposite.

items.prompt: Was the tower steady?
items.passage: Leo's tall tower of blocks swayed back and forth and then crashed to the floor.
items.hint: Did the tower stay firm?
items.explanation: Steady means firm and not wobbling. The tower swayed and fell, so it was not steady.

words.definition: to talk with too much pride about yourself or what you have

hero.text: Bolt began to boast about how fast he was, until Kai beat him in a race.

words.everyday: Jen likes to boast about her new shoes to everyone she meets.

contrast.nonExample: When Amir won the art prize, he said "Thank you" and praised the other artists.
contrast.explanation: To boast is to brag too much about yourself. Amir was modest and praised others, so he did not boast.

items.prompt: Which person is boasting?

options.text: Kyle says, "I'm the best player ever, way better than all of you!"
Kyle says, "Could you please help me practice my free throws after school?"

items.hint: Who talks about himself with too much pride?
items.explanation: To boast is to brag. Saying "I'm the best player ever" is bragging.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Mia loves to ___ about her high test scores, which bothers her friends.
items.clue: about her high test scores; bothers her friends
items.hint: What kind of talking about yourself bothers friends?
items.explanation: Talking about her own high scores in a way that "bothers her friends" is bragging. That is boasting.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "boasts" in this sentence?
items.passage: Uncle Joe always boasts about the giant fish he caught.
items.hint: How does Uncle Joe talk about his giant fish?
items.explanation: Brags means the same as boasts: talking proudly about yourself or what you did.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows the opposite of boasting.

chunks.text: Instead of boasting about her win,
thanked her coach and her team.
shouted that she was the greatest ever.

items.hint: "Instead of boasting" means she did NOT brag.
items.explanation: Thanking others is the opposite of boasting, so it fits "instead of boasting." Shouting that she was the greatest IS boasting.

items.prompt: Is Liz boasting?
items.passage: After scoring a goal, Liz ran around shouting, "Nobody can kick like me! I'm the best!"
items.hint: Is Liz talking about herself with too much pride?
items.explanation: Shouting "Nobody can kick like me! I'm the best!" is bragging about herself. That is boasting.
